Rashi on Pesachim 21a:10:1.hebrew: כל שעה שאוכל מאכיל מבעי ליה - אבל השתא דנקט לה בתרי לישני, משמע דאתרי גברי קאי. והא ליכא למימר דהכי קאמר: כל שעה שמותר לאכול מן התורה — מאכיל אפילו מדרבנן, ותיתוקם אליבא דר' יהודה — דהא איכא שש, דמותר לאכול מן התורה ואסור להאכיל לדברי הכל:
Rashi on Pesachim 21a:10:1.english: It should have said: "For the entire time that one eats, he may feed" - But now that it formulated it in two [different] expressions, it implies that it refers to two people. And one cannot say that this is what it is saying: "For the entire time that it is permitted to eat by Torah law, one may feed even by rabbinic law," and [thus] it would be established in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda — for behold, there is the sixth [hour], when it is permitted to eat by Torah law, yet forbidden to feed according to everyone.

Rashi on Pesachim 21a:11:1.hebrew: אלא הכי קאמר כל שעה - שיש היתר לשום אדם לאכול, מאכיל אף האסור לאכול לבהמתו, כו':
Rashi on Pesachim 21a:11:1.english: Rather, this is what it is saying: For the entire time - That there is permission for any person to eat, even one who is forbidden to eat may feed [it] to his animal, etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 21a:12:1.hebrew: בהמה אי משיירא חזי ליה - שאין דרכה להצניע, אבל חיה — כגון חולדה ונמיה וחתול — דרכן להצניע:
Rashi on Pesachim 21a:12:1.english: A domesticated animal, if it leaves over, he sees it - For it is not its manner to hide [food]; but non-domesticated animals — such as a weasel, a mongoose, and a cat — it is their manner to hide [food].

Rashi on Pesachim 21a:13:1.hebrew: ואי תנא חיה - הוה אמינא: היא עדיפא, משום דאי משיירא מצנעא לה, ולא עבר עליה בבל יראה:
Rashi on Pesachim 21a:13:1.english: And had it taught [about] a wild animal - I would have said [that] it is preferable, because if it leaves [food] over, it hides it, and he does not violate “it shall not be seen” on its account.

Rashi on Pesachim 21a:13:2.english: And [it is] not on his mind - To nullify it.

Rashi on Pesachim 21a:15:1.hebrew: קודם - שיבוא הפסח, דקסברי: מצוה עליו לבערו מן העולם, ולא שיהא קיים:
Rashi on Pesachim 21a:15:1.english: Before - [Before] Passover arrives; for they hold that it is a mitzvah upon him to eliminate it from the world, and not that it should remain in existence.

Rashi on Pesachim 21a:1:1.hebrew: אין הכרעת שלישית מכרעת - דעת שלישית היא זו, שבית שמאי ובית הלל לא הזכירו לגלות דעתם דניהוי חיישינן לתקלה כלל. דאי הוו אמרו הכי: ב"ש אומרים בין בבית בין בשדה חבל תשפך, וב"ה אומרים בין בבית בין בשדה תיעשה זילוף, ואתה בא להכריע ולומר: בבית כב"ה, בשדה כבית שמאי — הויא הכרעה. אבל השתא דלא הזכירו בית ושדה, טעמא אחרינא הוא ולאו משום תקלה, ור' ישמעאל חייש לתקלה — והיינו תנאי:
Rashi on Pesachim 21a:1:1.english: The decision of a third [opinion] is not a decision - This is a third opinion [entirely], for Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not mention [anything] to disclose their opinion that we should be concerned about a mishap at all. For had they said as follows: Beit Shammai say [that] whether in the house or in the field, it shall be poured out to waste, and Beit Hillel say [that] whether in the house or in the field, it shall be used for sprinkling, and you were coming to decide [between them] and say: in the house like Beit Hillel, [and] in the field like Beit Shammai — that would be a [valid] decision. But now that they did not mention house or field, [their] reason is another [matter] and not because of a mishap, whereas Rabbi Yishmael is concerned about a mishap; and this is [a dispute between] Tannaim.

Rashi on Pesachim 21a:2:1.hebrew: מחלוקת - ר' אליעזר ור' יהושע, שנפלה לפחות ממאה חולין טמאים — שיש בגת התחתונה פחות ממאה חולין טמאים, דאין תרומה בטילה בהן ופסדי לגמרי, דתרומה צריך אחד ומאה לבטלה. אבל היו בתחתונה מאה חולין — מאה חביות כמו זו של תרומה — דברי הכל לא יטמאה ביד, הואיל ולא פסדי חולין, דתרומה עולה בהן, וחזו בימי טומאה כדמעיקרא לזר:
Rashi on Pesachim 21a:2:1.english: The dispute - [Between] Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua [applies to a case] where it fell into less than one hundred [se'ah of] impure non-sacred [wine]: that there is in the lower press less than one hundred [measures of] impure non-sacred [wine], so that the teruma is not nullified in them and they are completely ruined, as teruma requires one and one hundred [parts] to be nullified. But had there been in the lower [press] one hundred [measures of] non-sacred [wine] — one hundred barrels like this one of teruma — all agree that he may not defile it by hand, since the non-sacred [wine] is not ruined, as the teruma is neutralized in them, and they are fit during [one's] days of impurity just as from the outset for a non-priest.

Rashi on Pesachim 21a:4:1.hebrew: מודה ר' אליעזר כו' - קס"ד אמסקנא קאי: אאם לאו, דהא פלוגתייהו באם לאו הוא. ולהכי פריך: "מודה ר' יהושע, דאמר לעיל 'יטמאנה ביד', לר' אליעזר, דאמר 'לא יטמאנה ביד' — מיבעי ליה למיתני":
Rashi on Pesachim 21a:4:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer concedes, etc. - [The Gemara] initially assumed that [this] refers to the conclusion: to “And if not,” for their dispute is regarding “And if not.” And that is why [the Gemara] challenges: It should have taught: “Rabbi Yehoshua — who said above, ‘He may actively render it impure with [his] hand’ — concedes to Rabbi Eliezer — who said, ‘He may not actively render it impure with [his] hand’!”

Rashi on Pesachim 21a:6:1.hebrew: בכלי שתוכו טהור וגבו טמא - והאי מודה לאו אסיפא קאי, אלא ארישא — דקתני: אם יכול להציל רביעית בטהרה יציל, ואפי' כלי זה שהוא בא להציל רביעית זו בתוכו — תוכו טהור וגבו טמא. ואשמעינן ליה לר' אליעזר, דאמר: "אל יטמאנה ביד" — מודה הוא דמותר להציל בזה, ולא חיישינן דילמא נגע גבו בתרומה ומטמא לה בידים. ובכלי שנטמא במשקין, דטומאתן דרבנן היא דמשכחת לה, כדתניא: כלי שנטמאו אחוריו במשקין — אחוריו טמאין, תוכו או אוגנו או אזנו או ידיו טהורין:
Rashi on Pesachim 21a:6:1.english: In a vessel whose interior is pure and whose exterior is impure - And this [statement that Rabbi Eliezer] "concedes" refers not to the latter clause [of the baraita], but to the first clause, which teaches: "If he is able to rescue a quarter-[log] in ritual purity, he should rescue [it]," and even [if] this vessel, into which he is coming to rescue this quarter-[log], its interior is pure and its exterior is impure. And it teaches us concerning Rabbi Eliezer, who said: "One should not render it impure with [one's] hand," that he concedes that it is permitted to rescue [the teruma] with this [vessel], and we do not suspect lest its exterior touch the teruma and he [thereby] render it impure with [his] hands. And it is found in [the case of] a vessel that became impure through liquids, whose impurity is rabbinic, as it is taught [in a baraita]: "A vessel whose exterior became impure through liquids — its exterior is impure; its interior, or its rim, or its handle, or its grips are pure."

Rashi on Pesachim 21a:8:1.hebrew: כל שעה שמותר לאכול מאכיל - לדוקייא איצטריך, דתידוק: הא משעה שאינו מותר לאכול — אינו מותר להאכיל:
Rashi on Pesachim 21a:8:1.english: For the entire time that it is permitted to eat, one may feed - It was necessary [to state this] for an inference, so that you infer: But from the time that it is not permitted to eat, it is not permitted to feed.

Rashi on Pesachim 21a:8:2.hebrew: ולא יסיק בו תנור וכירים - בגמרא פריך: פשיטא, הא נמי הנאה היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 21a:8:2.english: And one may not light an oven or a stove with it - In the Gemara, it asks: [Isn't this] obvious? This too is benefit.

Tosafot on Pesachim 21a:13:1.hebrew: ואי אשמעינן חיה משום דמצנעא לה - ואין עובר משום בל יטמין, דבל יטמין נפקא לן מ"לא ימצא", ואין זה מצוי כיון שאין ידוע היכן הוא. וכן משמע בפ"ק (דף ו:) דפריך: "וכי משכחת לה ליבטלה?", משמע דכל כמה דלא משכחת לא עבר בבל יראה. הק' רשב"א: היכי שרי להאכיל לחיה שדרכה להטמין? הא תנן בפ"ק (דף ט:): "מה שמשייר יניחנו בצינעא, כדי שלא תטול חולדה בפניו ויהא צריך בדיקה אחריו", וכ"ש שאסור ליתן בפניהם! ויש לחלק בין חיה לחולדה: המגדלים בבתים — דההיא לא מצנעא כולי האי כמו חולדה, הטומנת בחורים ובסדקין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 21a:13:1.english: "And had it informed us of a wild animal, because it conceals it" - And he does not violate [the prohibition] on account of "you shall not conceal" [bal yatmin], for [the prohibition of] "bal yatmin" is derived by us from [the verse]: "It shall not be found" (Exodus 12:19), and this is not "found" [i.e., discoverable], since it is not known where it is. And so it is implied in the first chapter (6b), where [the Gemara] asks: "And when you find it, let him nullify it!" — implying that as long as you do not find it, one does not violate [the prohibition]: "It shall not be seen." The Rashba [Rabbeinu Shimshon of Sens] asked: How is it permitted to feed a wild animal whose nature is to conceal [its food]? Didn't we learn in the first chapter (9a): "What he leaves over he should place in concealment, so that a weasel will not take [it] before him, and he will require another search after it"? And all the more so that it should be forbidden to place [food directly] before them! And one can distinguish between a [wild] animal and a weasel: [with regard to an animal] of those that are raised in houses, that one does not conceal [food] so much as a weasel, which conceals [it] in holes and crevices.

Tosafot on Pesachim 21a:13:2.hebrew: וקאי עליה בבל יראה - פי': אם לא ביטלו. והוא הדין דהוה מצי למימר: דילמא אתי למיכל מיניה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 21a:13:2.english: "And [the prohibition] 'it shall not be seen' applies to him" - Explanation: [This applies] if he did not nullify it. And likewise, [the Gemara] could have said: Lest he come to eat from it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 21a:1:1.hebrew: אין הכרעת שלישית מכרעת - פ"ה: הואיל ולא הזכירו בית שמאי ובית הלל בית ושדה, א"כ טעמא אחרינא הוא, ולא משום תקלה. ולר"י נראה: אע"ג דטעמא דבית שמאי משום תקלה, לא חשיב הכרעה, לפי שלא גילו הראשונים דעתן לחלק בין בית לשדה, שלא הזכירו בדבריהם אחד בית ואחד שדה. וכן פ"ה לעיל גבי ר"ג: "לאו מכריע הוא". וההיא דקולי מטלניות: "בין מן המוכן ובין שלא מן המוכן טמא", דברי ר"א, ר' יהושע אומר: "בין מן המוכן ובין שלא מן המוכן טהור", ר"ע אומר: "מן המוכן טמא, שלא מן המוכן טהור" — וחשיב ליה בפ' כירה (שבת לט: ושם) הכרעה, שהרי גילו ר' אליעזר ור' יהושע דשייך לחלק בין מן המוכן ובין שלא מן המוכן. וההיא דפ' כיצד מברכין (ברכות מג:), דקאמר ב"ש: "מברכים על השמן", וקאמר ר"ג: "אני אכריע: שמן — זכינו לריחו וזכינו לסיכתו, הדס — לריחו זכינו, לסיכתו לא זכינו", וקאמר רבי יוחנן: "הלכה כדברי המכריע" — לאו משום דמכריע גמור הוא, אלא מפרש ונותן טעם לדבריו. ותדע, דאי מכריע הוא, למה הוצרך לפסוק הלכה כמותו? הא כבר א"ר יוחנן בפרק כירה: "הלכה כדברי המכריע"! וק"ק לפי' זה: דהכא מאי איריא הכרעה שלישית שאין הכרעה? תיפוק ליה דהכרעת תלמיד לאו הכרעה היא, כדאמר בפ' כירה (שבת לט:) ארבי עקיבא! ור"ח פי': הכרעת שלישית — דור שלישי, דהיינו הכרעת תלמיד, כדאמר בפ' כירה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 21a:1:1.english: "The decision of a third [opinion] is not a decision" - Rashi explained: Since Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not mention "house" and "field", if so, [their dispute] is for another reason and not due to [concern for] a stumbling block. And it appears to Ri: Even if Beit Shammai's reason is due to [concern for] a stumbling block, it is not considered a [valid] compromise decision, because the first [disputants] did not reveal their view to distinguish between house and field, for they did not mention in their words either house or field. And similarly Rashi explained earlier regarding [the statement], "Rabban Gamliel is not a compromiser." And that [case] of small patches: "Whether from that which was prepared or from that which was not prepared, it is ritually impure," [these are] the words of Rabbi Eliezer; Rabbi Yehoshua says: "Whether from that which was prepared or from that which was not prepared, it is ritually pure"; Rabbi Akiva says: "From that which was prepared, it is impure; from that which was not prepared, it is pure" — and [the Gemara] in the chapter [entitled] Kira (Shabbat 39b and there) considers it a [valid] compromise decision, for Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua had indeed revealed that it is relevant to distinguish between that which was prepared and that which was not prepared. And that [case] in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Mevarkhin (Berakhot 43b), where Beit Shammai say: "One recites the blessing over the oil," and Rabban Gamliel says: "I will decide: [With regard to] oil, we benefit from its fragrance and we benefit from its anointing; [with regard to] myrtle, we benefit from its fragrance, [but] we do not benefit from its anointing," and Rabbi Yochanan says: "The halakha is in accordance with the words of the compromiser" — [this is] not because he is a full-fledged compromiser, but rather [Rabbi Yochanan] is explaining and providing a rationale for his words. And know [that this is so], for if he were a [standard] compromiser, why did [Rabbi Yochanan] need to rule the halakha in accordance with him? Did not Rabbi Yochanan already say in the chapter [entitled] Kira: "The halakha is in accordance with the words of the compromiser"? And it is slightly difficult according to this explanation: Here, why specifically [did they say that] a third decision is not a decision? Let him derive it [from the fact] that a student's compromise is not a compromise, as [the Gemara] said in the chapter [entitled] Kira (Shabbat 39b) regarding Rabbi Akiva! And Rabbeinu Chananel explained: "A third decision" [means the decision of] a third generation, which is [the equivalent of] a student's compromise, as [the Gemara] said in the chapter [entitled] Kira.

Tosafot on Pesachim 21a:8:1.hebrew: כל שעה. עבר זמנו אסור בהנאה - ואסור למכור; ואם מכר — דמיו מותרין, דאין תופס את דמיו, כדתנן בפ"ב דקדושין (דף נו:): מכרן וקידש בדמיהן — מקודשת:
Tosafot on Pesachim 21a:8:1.english: "For the entire time. [Once] its time passes, it is prohibited to derive benefit [from it]" - And it is prohibited to sell [it]; but if he sold [it], its proceeds are permitted, for [chametz] does not transfer its prohibition to its proceeds, as we learned in a Mishnah in the second chapter of Kiddushin (56b): "[If] he sold them and betrothed [a woman] with their proceeds, she is betrothed."

Tosafot on Pesachim 21a:9:1.hebrew: לימא מתניתין דלא כר' יהודה - אף לפי המסקנא לא אתיא כר' יהודה, אלא הכי קאמר: לימא מתני' דלא כר' יהודה, אלא כר' מאיר? ומסיק דכר' מאיר נמי לא אתי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 21a:9:1.english: "Let us say that the Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda" - Even according to the conclusion, [the Mishnah] does not accord with Rabbi Yehuda. Rather, this is what [the Gemara] is saying: "Shall we say that the Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, but rather in accordance with Rabbi Meir?" And [the Gemara] concludes that it does not accord with Rabbi Meir either.
